title: The N-2 assertion for a power series ring
statement: Let R be a Noetherian integral domain which is N-2. Then the one-variable power series ring R[[x]] is N-2.

proof.text: Put A = integralClosure R (FractionRing R). Applying hR to the fraction field makes A finite over R. Mathlib IsNoetherianRing.of_finite and integralClosure.isIntegrallyClosedOfFiniteExtension give that A is Noetherian and normal; it is a domain as a subalgebra of a field. The coefficient inclusion is injective, so N-2 ascends to A by the finite-domain-extension lemma.

Prove coefficientwise finiteness in the private Lean helper finite_power_series_extension. Choose a finite generating family s_i of A over R. For a series f and each k, express its coefficient as sum_i c_{k,i} s_i. Form the scalar series g_i with coefficient c_{k,i} at k. Equality of coefficients proves f = sum_i g_i C(s_i), so the constant series C(s_i) generate A[[x]] over R[[x]]. This is an explicit proof, with no postponed lemma.

The normal-power-series theorem makes A[[x]] normal, and Mathlib supplies its Noetherian and x-adic completeness instances. In the private helper isN2_quotient_X, identify A[[x]]/(x) with A: Ideal.mem_span_singleton and PowerSeries.X_dvd_iff identify (x) with the kernel of constantCoeff, which is surjective since constantCoeff(C(a)) = a. RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective gives the equivalence. Its inverse is an injective finite algebra map, so the finite-domain-extension ascent theorem transfers N-2 to the quotient. The prime-ideal theorem PowerSeries.span_X_isPrime supplies its domain instance. Tate's principal-complete criterion, applied to x = PowerSeries.X, now gives N-2 of A[[x]].

The coefficientwise map R[[x]] to A[[x]] is injective by PowerSeries.map_injective applied to the coefficient inclusion. Apply the finite-domain-extension descent theorem with the finiteness proved in the second step, and N-2 of A[[x]] from the third step, to conclude N-2 of R[[x]].
